summary:
BG2 Thanksgiving roundtable (Nov 2024): each host raises topics of the week. Gurley on China's tech progress, IPO compounding ratchets, instant government payment rails (Pix, FedNow) and Anthropic's open-source MCP; Gerstner on DOGE budget arithmetic, EV credit vs gas tax, tariffs as anchoring negotiation, Buffett's giving and Invest America.
Mostly policy opinion; limited testable market mechanism; fiscal arithmetic and tariff-as-negotiation views are the main takeaways.

coverage.note: China STEM and tariffs; DOGE and budget-balancing arithmetic
revenue growth scenarios, Argentina ETF, IPO ratchet
ratchet incentives, down-round IPOs, Newsom EV credit
EV credit vs gas tax, Pix/FedNow payments, Visa/MC margins
payment rails and lobbying, tariffs on Canada/Mexico
tariffs as anchoring, MCP open source
open source strategy, pre-training scaling, Buffett letter
effective giving idea (no claim), conspiracy-theory labeling
Invest America funding and timeline, outro

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the rumors and the Articles suggest that they have accomplished fairly high-end semiconductor manufacturing at smic in China
claims.claim: Huawei's Mate 70 reportedly runs a non-Android OS on a chip made at SMIC, not TSMC, suggesting China has achieved high-end chip manufacturing despite export controls.
claims.testable: partly - verify chip node and yields

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I think American exceptionalism has gotten into our
claims.claim: US complacency about its technology lead is a competitiveness risk, because pretending China cannot be cut off or is behind is unhelpful.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the air economy is likely to be two perhaps three times larger than that of the us
claims.claim: Citing Elon Musk, China's economy may become two to three times the size of the US, and since war's foundation is economic, the US is like a long-time biggest kid facing a much bigger one.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the number of graduates in China's University system that are stem is 35% and that number is below 10 in the US
claims.claim: China produces a much larger share of STEM graduates (35% vs below 10% in the US), and with work ethic gives it the pieces to run fast.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: tariffs and protectionism will only protect American industry for a very short window
claims.claim: Tariffs and technology blocks (ASML, AI) protect US industry only briefly and remove the competition US firms need.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: an idea that we can totally decouple from the second largest economy in the world is one that's probably not wise
claims.claim: The US should focus on running its own race as fast as possible, without naivety about China's intentions, but full decoupling from the second largest economy is unwise.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: a $38 trillion debt and a$2 trillion deficit frankly is just unconscionable
claims.claim: US debt of about $38T and a $2T deficit are an unethical burden on future generations, financed by borrowing and a levered Fed balance sheet.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if you reduced spending for the next four years bill at 3% it simply gets us back to 6 trillion
claims.claim: Cutting spending about 3% a year for four years returns outlays from the $7T COVID bump to the roughly $6T 15-year trend line, which is not draconian.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it assumes that revenues grow at 3 and a half% and if we do that then we balance the budget in 2029
claims.claim: With revenues growing 3.5% a year and spending cut back to trend (about $6T), the budget balances in 2029.
claims.conditions: assumes 3.5% revenue growth and spending cuts

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if we grew revenues at the same rate that we have for the last 20 years right starting next year which is 4.9% per year keger for 20 years we would end up with a $450 billion Surplus in 2029
claims.claim: At the 20-year revenue growth rate (4.9% CAGR) with spending back on trend the US would reach a $450B surplus in 2029, and about $700B at the 5.8% pace since the 2017 tax cuts.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: since the tax cuts in 20197 we've grown our federal revenues at 5.8%
claims.claim: Federal revenues grew faster after the 2017 tax cuts (5.8% vs 4.9%), arguing that tax cuts do not necessarily lower revenue.
claims.indicator: federal revenue growth after 2017 tax cuts
claims.testable: partly - confounded by growth and inflation

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: argt it's up 60% year-to date 65
claims.claim: The Argentina ETF ARGT is up about 60% YTD after Milei's reforms, showing optimism reversing and supporting the doability of large spending cuts.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: it allows a company to pretend that the cover price on a term sheet is whatever they want it to be
claims.claim: A compounding IPO ratchet hides investor returns in the IPO clause rather than the price, letting a company show a headline valuation while guaranteeing late investors a return.
claims.indicator: IPO ratchet clauses in late-stage rounds
claims.testable: partly - requires S-1 cap table review

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: the later stage investors that wrote this uh compounding ratchet term actually want the IPO to be as low as possible because they'll they'll get more shares
claims.claim: The ratchet makes late-stage investors prefer a low IPO price (more shares at the expense of employees, founders and earlier investors), a misalignment.
claims.testable: partly - IPO pricing vs ratchet presence

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I suspect these late stage investors are going to be tugging on the ear of the bankers rooting for an even lower price
claims.claim: IPO underpricing already has many incentives, and the ratchet adds another for the late-stage investors to lobby for a lower price.
claims.testable: yes - first-day returns for ratchet IPOs

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: so they do these to avoid it but it comes home to roost and you concentrate risk
claims.claim: Companies accept such terms to avoid a down round, but it concentrates risk and can lead to negative outcomes later.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: if the market in 20 21 was overheated and prices were really high in the private markets that's just a fact of life that's a fact of zerp that's a fact of 0% interest rates
claims.claim: Private valuations in 2021 were inflated by zero interest rates, so a down-round IPO simply reprices to the moment and companies should go public when it is time.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: may actually be what's creating the incentive to go public
claims.claim: The annual crank on the ratchet may push the company to IPO sooner, as a similar situation did at Square.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: Nome has proposed an EV tax credit Revival if Trump cuts the federal EV tax credit which many many observers say we should cut at this point in time it's no longer needed
claims.claim: California's proposal to revive an EV credit excluding Tesla (about 550,000 cars made in Fremont) is politically foolish; the federal credit is no longer needed.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: an EV credit costs the government money you just spoke about us not having a balanced budget a increased gas tax would actually bring in income
claims.claim: A gas tax is better policy than an EV credit because it raises revenue and taxes the negative rather than paying for desired behavior, which creates perverse behavior.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: when gas prices spiked in 2009 uh uh big SUV sales went in the tank
claims.claim: Evidence for price-driven behavior: SUV sales collapsed when gasoline spiked in 2009, which is why Europe has small cars, so taxing fuel moves consumers to electric.
claims.direction: SUV demand falls when gas price rises

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: is already up to I think 43% of all payments in Brazil
claims.claim: Brazil's government-run instant payment system Pix reached about 43% of all payments within a few years, mirroring UK Faster Payments, India UPI and others, while the US lags (ACH takes days).

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: Visa and MasterCard have the two highest operating margin percentages in our markets total like they're over 60%
claims.claim: Visa and MasterCard's operating margins above 60% show an oligopoly the US fails to challenge, and instant public rails threaten those margins.
claims.direction: instant payment rails negative for card networks

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I think it's because of regulatory capture the banks don't want it vison MasterCard don't want it
claims.claim: The US has not built an instant payment system because of regulatory capture by banks and card networks, though FedNow is underway (B2B first).

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: it's clear in these other countries that letting the government do this one part and getting it right leads to all kinds of fintech innovation because you can transfer money quickly
claims.claim: A government-run instant payment rail enables fintech and crypto innovation on top, and single-provider infrastructure is natural, whereas private provision leads to excessive margins.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: visa mcard and the banks will lean on every one of their representatives in Washington and fight it all the way
claims.claim: Incumbent card networks and banks will lobby hard against FedNow, and innovators often hate innovation that threatens their position (as in clean tech).

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: one of his first acts will be to initiate a 25% tariff on products coming from Canada and Mexico unless they get serious about stopping illegal immigrants and drugs from crossing the border
claims.claim: Trump announced a 25% tariff on Canada and Mexico, while Bessent said the tariff gun will be loaded but rarely discharged.
claims.indicator: US tariffs on Canada and Mexico

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: treat them as effective negotiating tactics not as literary flourishes
claims.claim: Tariff threats should be taken as effective negotiating tactics, not literary flourishes, contrary to consensus that they are not serious.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: it is a starting point he's going to raise these tariffs in order to achieve National objectives and then he's going to be willing to negotiate away from them
claims.claim: Tariffs work like anchoring in negotiation: set a high starting point, then trade it away for national objectives; the speaker dislikes tariffs economically but sees them as a tactic.
claims.testable: partly - compare threats to final tariffs

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the thing about Trump is I don't think it's a bluff
claims.claim: The tariff threats are credible, e.g. fentanyl precursors flow from China via Mexico, so the ask is reasonable and the threat is not a bluff.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: anthropic released a a new data connection tool
claims.claim: Anthropic open-sourced MCP, a data connection protocol, as a strategic competitive tool (like Meta's Open Compute Project and Google's Kubernetes) to avoid proprietary connectors from rivals.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: it has definitely become a strategic tool for everyone out there
claims.claim: Open source has become a strategic weapon for large technology firms that removes IP control from competitors.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: I think it is one of the most Savvy competitive weapons you can bring to the field
claims.claim: Open-sourcing a standard is a savvy competitive tactic against a rival that might create proprietary connectors, and should boost AI innovation and competition.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: Bill is talking a lot about the deceleration and the rate of pre-scaling or uh pre-training um uh scaling
claims.claim: Discussion of the deceleration of pre-training scaling coincided with a down day for Nvidia, per CNBC commentary, indicating AI-scaling worries move Nvidia.
claims.direction: Nvidia down on scaling slowdown talk

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: the real action from compounding takes place in the final 20 years of a lifetime
claims.claim: Buffett letter: the bulk of compounding gain occurs in the last 20 years of a lifetime, hence holding long.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: given away versus preserved for building dynasties
claims.claim: The US may be the first nation where most top 1-2% wealth is given away rather than kept in dynasties, which flows back into consumer surplus.

claims.speaker: Bill Gurley
claims.quote: you got to treat them both as if they did happen
claims.claim: For root-cause analysis under uncertainty (COVID origins) treat both competing hypotheses as real, and avoid labelling dissent a conspiracy theory.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: would cause to created 3.7 million investment accounts a year uh for every child that's born in America
claims.claim: Invest America would create about 3.7M investment accounts a year, one per newborn, seeded by government and topped up by companies and parents (a 401k from birth).

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: they're more likely to graduate from high school more likely to graduate from college more likely to buy a home more likely to start a business
claims.claim: Research with the Milken Institute finds funded accounts raise educational attainment, home ownership, entrepreneurship, and financial literacy and reduce incarceration, a structural rebalancing from state to individual.

claims.speaker: Brad Gerstner
claims.quote: put into uh the reconciliation process in the spring
claims.claim: Expectation that Invest America can be put into the spring 2025 reconciliation process; wealthy donors could also match contributions via drawdown trusts investing in the S&P 500.
